open_points.subject: MCP get_repair_view paging behavior
open_points.text: A16 rule 6: "Every list operation returns `page_size_default` items unless the caller asks for another size" versus State 5 MCP catalogue for `get_repair_view`: "no continuation, every list at `page_size_max`"
open_points.question: Is `get_repair_view` exempt from A16 list paging rules, or must it follow caller-sized/default paging like other list operations?
options: Treat `get_repair_view` as a special fixed-size read (always `page_size_max`, no continuation)
Treat `get_repair_view` lists as normal paged lists (`page_size_default` unless caller specifies)
open_points.default_guess: Treat `get_repair_view` as a special fixed-size read, because State 5 states that behavior explicitly.

open_points.subject: Timestamp meaning for execution/attempt records
open_points.text: State 5 convention: "Every timestamp an operation records comes from `clock.kernel_now`, taken once per store change."
open_points.question: For records that carry start/end fields (`started_at`, `ended_at`, `recorded_at`, `concluded_at`, `executed_at`), which exact event moment must each field represent when operations span time (sandbox run, HTTP send)?
options: Use one timestamp from the write change for all fields written in that change
Capture start at operation-begin and end at conclusion/write, passing both into the store change
open_points.default_guess: Capture start when execution/send begins and end when it concludes, then persist those explicit moments.
